:::{#def-median-survival}
#### Median survival time

Given a random time-to-event variable $T$ with
survival function $\surv(t)$ (@def-surv-fn)
and inverse survival function $\surv^{-1}(p)$ (@def-inv-surv-fn),
the **median survival time** $t_{\text{med}}$
is the earliest time by which the survival probability
has fallen to or below one half:

$$t_{\text{med}} \eqdef \surv^{-1}(0.5) = \inf\cb{t \ge 0 : \surv(t) \le 0.5}.$$

[@klein2003survival, Chapter 2]
:::

::: notes
When $\surv(t)$ is continuous and strictly decreasing,
$t_{\text{med}}$ is the unique time at which $\surv(t_{\text{med}}) = 0.5$:
half of the population has experienced the event by $t_{\text{med}}$,
and half has not.
:::
